svg.text: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ DL, with NLP cutting across them — and Gen AI as a newer, separate job
AI
ML
DL
NLP
NLP is not a subset — it's a job (language) that AI/ML/DL all get applied to.
Full definitions, start dates, and examples are in the cards →
AI — Artificial Intelligence
Definition: making a computer act smart — with or without learning. Can be pure
hand-written rules; AI is the goal, not one specific method.
Started: 1956 — the term was coined at the Dartmouth Workshop.
Example: Deep Blue (1997) beat the world chess champion using hand-coded rules
and brute-force search — zero learning involved.
ML — Machine Learning
Definition: a subset of AI — the computer learns patterns from data instead of
being told rules by a human. Needs data + a way to check if it's learning correctly.
Started: 1959 — term coined by Arthur Samuel (self-playing checkers program).
Example: a spam filter trained on a million emails already labeled "spam" /
"not spam" — it works out the pattern itself.
DL — Deep Learning
Definition: a subset of ML using multi-layer "neural networks." Great at messy,
raw data (images, audio, text) where you can't hand-write what "the pattern" is.
Started: idea from 1943; took off in 2012 when AlexNet won an image contest big.
Example: a CNN reads raw X-ray pixels directly and flags a tumor — nobody
hand-picks "look for a round white shape," the network learns that itself.
NLP — Natural Language Processing
Definition: NOT a subset of AI/ML/DL — it's a job/domain: making computers
understand and use human language. Done via rules, ML, or DL.
Started: 1950 — Alan Turing's "Can machines think?" and the Turing Test.
Example: Google Translate — rule-based (2006) → statistical → today's
transformer-based model, far more natural.
Gen AI — Generative AI
Definition: not "sort/predict" like classic ML/DL — it CREATES new content
(text, image, audio, video, code) that didn't exist before. Built on DL.
Started: 2014 GANs; went mainstream 2020–22 (GPT-3, DALL-E, ChatGPT).
Example: ChatGPT writes an email; Stable Diffusion turns a text prompt into
a photorealistic image.
Interview one-liner: AI is the goal; ML/DL are two nested strategies to reach it; NLP is the language domain; Gen AI is the newest job — creating, not just predicting.
